tagline: The shared base every Xios desktop flavor builds on
description:
**xios-core** is the shared base for the fullscreen Xios desktops. It installs the Xios display app (Home Screen icon **X11**), the iosc compositor and iosc-shell, `xios-session` (which starts, stops and switches desktops), and **xios-launcher-tools**, whose ioscd daemon is what the in-app desktop picker talks to. Through **xios-runtime** it also brings the ANGLE GPU stack (OpenGL ES on Metal), the D-Bus message bus, desktop audio, and the defaults for fonts, locale, and paths.

You normally do not install this package directly. Pick a flavor instead and it pulls xios-core in:

- **xios-gnome**: GNOME Shell on Mutter
- **xios-kde**: KDE Plasma Desktop, Mobile and Nano on KWin
- **xios-x11**: X11 apps through rootless Xwayland on the iosc desktop

**xios-native** (Linux apps as regular iPadOS windows) does not use xios-core.

The display app is unsigned, so it needs **AppSync Unified** (from the https://cydia.akemi.ai/ repo) to launch.

changelog.notes: - Requires the fixed xios-session (1.0.82) and xios-launcher-tools (0.1.12)
- Installs xios-launcher-tools again. 0.1.6 through 0.1.11 left it out, so on a clean install there was no ioscd and every desktop pick in the app failed with "ioscd timed out" (GitHub issue #11)

- Installs the Xios display app (com.max.xios): no more sideloading it by hand
- Every flavor now brings its own display: install one package and open X11 on the Home Screen
- First release: iosc + ANGLE + D-Bus + audio + desktop defaults as one base package
